- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing sharp reversals.
- After a price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from bearish to bullish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate from 3rd period onward using sentiment-weighted moving average.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-period moving average of forecast vs true is consistently >1.5% above true, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per period.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period spikes (last 5–7 days); apply “late-period bump” rule: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment >0.6 and true > forecast by 2%+ in prior period.
